\chapter{Saying No}
\label{ch:mw-saying-no}
\hlchaptermodality{39}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can refuse an offer in Marwadi and leave a bargain open, which the market chapters could not do.}

The refusal and the walk-away run in all four skills, against the counter-offer the market chapters had no answer to.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[konī]{Hear \emph{konī} — no}

\label{lesson:MW-C39-hear-koni}



\begin{quote}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Recall:} say \textbf{\mw{हां} \mw{सा}}, the respectful yes — the answer this book has had since chapter 3 and never given a partner
  \item \emph{Recall:} write \textbf{\mw{अठारा}} — \textbf{R2}
  \item \emph{Recall:} write \textbf{\mw{बारा}} — \textbf{R3}
\end{itemize}
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\begin{quote}
\emph{konī} — \textbf{no}, \textbf{not}
\end{quote}

Chapter 3 taught \textbf{\mw{हां} \mw{सा}} and stopped there. Every chapter since — the market, the food stall, the rickshaw — has given you ways to ask, to offer and to agree, and no way at all to decline. A course that can name a price and cannot refuse one has only half a bargain in it.

\emph{Konī} is the word. Two beats, both light: \emph{ko-nī}.

It is worth knowing that this word is one of the things that makes Marwari Marwari. Hindi says \emph{nahī̃}; a Swadesh word list collected for Marwari gives \emph{konī} for \textquotedblleft{}not\textquotedblright{}. Say \emph{konī} in Rajasthan and you are not speaking Hindi with an accent.

Keep your pencil down: the spelling is the next lesson's, and it needs no sign you have not already made.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Sources: \href{https://selindia.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/SWL-Marwari\_IPA.pdf}{SEL India, Swadesh Word List — Marwari Language, entry 16}; \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-9-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 9}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[konī]{\mw{कोनी} — no, on the page}

\label{lesson:MW-C39-koni}



\begin{quote}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Recall:} say \emph{konī} before you look at it — \textbf{R1}
  \item \emph{Recall:} write \textbf{\mw{ए}}, the letter the first number needed — \textbf{R4}
  \item \emph{Recall:} write \textbf{\mw{उ}} — \textbf{R2}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say \textbf{terā} — \textbf{R3}
\end{itemize}
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\mw{को}} + \textbf{\mw{नी}} $\to$ \textbf{\mw{कोनी}} — \emph{konī} — no
\end{quote}

Two pieces, four signs, and not one of them is new. \textbf{\mw{क}} and \textbf{\mw{ो}} you have written since chapter 5; \textbf{\mw{न}} since chapter 5; \textbf{\mw{ी}} since chapter 4.

That is worth saying plainly, because it means this word cost the hand nothing and was missing anyway. The gap was never a writing problem.

\subsection*{Your turn}
Copy \textbf{\mw{कोनी}} once while looking. Then write \textbf{\mw{हां} \mw{सा}} above it and \textbf{\mw{कोनी}} below, so the yes and the no sit one over the other on the page for the first time in this book.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Sources: \href{https://selindia.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/SWL-Marwari\_IPA.pdf}{SEL India, Swadesh Word List — Marwari Language, entry 16}; \href{https://www.unicode.org/charts/PDF/U0900.pdf}{Unicode Devanagari chart}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[Practice]{\mw{दस} \mw{करो।} — \mw{कोनी।}}

\label{lesson:MW-R39-refuse-price}



\begin{quote}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Recall:} write \textbf{\mw{कोनी}} — \textbf{R1}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say \emph{ughaṇīs}, five lessons back, and say what it is built on — \textbf{R2}
  \item \emph{Recall:} write \textbf{\mw{तेरा}} — \textbf{R3}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say \textbf{ek} — \textbf{R4}
\end{itemize}
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Until now the counter-offer had no answer but agreement. Now it has two.

\begin{quote}
— \textbf{\mw{ये} \mw{कितणे} \mw{कू} \mw{है}?} — \emph{Ye kitṇe kū hai?} — How much is this? — \textbf{\mw{बीस।}} — \emph{Bīs.} — Twenty. — \textbf{\mw{दस} \mw{करो।}} — \emph{Das karo.} — Make it ten. — \textbf{\mw{कोनी।}} — \emph{Konī.} — No.
\end{quote}

Run it three times, changing only the two numbers, and use the teens you have just learned for at least one of them: \emph{satarā}, \emph{pandarā}, \emph{ughaṇīs}.

Then run it with the roles swapped, so you are the one who says \textbf{\mw{कोनी}}.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Sources: \href{https://selindia.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/SWL-Marwari\_IPA.pdf}{SEL India, Swadesh Word List — Marwari Language, entry 16}; \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-9-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 9}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[Practice]{Refuse, and leave}

\label{lesson:MW-C39-refusal-four}



\begin{quote}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Recall:} write \textbf{\mw{उघणीस}}, five lessons back — \textbf{R2}
  \item \emph{Recall:} write \textbf{\mw{एक}}, the first number this book taught — \textbf{R4}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say \textbf{caudā} — \textbf{R3}
\end{itemize}
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
A refusal in a bazaar is rarely the last word. It is followed by leaving — and the leaving line is one this book taught in chapter 7 and has not needed until now:

\begin{quote}
— \textbf{\mw{दस} \mw{करो।}} — \emph{Das karo.} — Make it ten. — \textbf{\mw{कोनी।}} — \emph{Konī.} — No. — \textbf{\mw{पाछे} \mw{मिलसू।}} — \emph{Pāchhe milsū.} — We'll meet later.
\end{quote}

\emph{Pāchhe milsū} was learned as a goodbye. In a market it is also a move: it says the bargain is not over, only paused, and it is what leaves the door open for the seller to call you back with a better number.

\subsection*{Your turn}
Four skills, one exchange.

\begin{enumerate}
\raggedright
  \item \textbf{Listen.} Hear a seller name a figure and an offer refused; say what the two numbers were.
  \item \textbf{Speak.} Run the exchange twice, once refusing and once agreeing, so the two branches sit side by side.
  \item \textbf{Read.} Read the three-turn refusal printed, and say the walk-away line aloud without looking.
  \item \textbf{Write.} Write \textbf{\mw{कोनी।}} and \textbf{\mw{पाछे} \mw{मिलसू।}} as two lines, and above them write the figure you were offered in words.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\end{tcolorbox}
\section[Practice]{Close the writing loop for \mw{इ}, \mw{ळ}, \mw{अ} and \mw{उ}}

\label{lesson:MW-R39-script-close}



\begin{quote}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Recall:} run the refusal and the walk-away once, from the lesson just before this — \textbf{R1}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say \emph{do}, two, and say which of its two meanings this is — \textbf{R4}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say \textbf{konī}
  \item \emph{Recall:} write \textbf{\mw{कोनी}} — \textbf{R1}
  \item \emph{Recall:} write \textbf{\mw{चौदा}} — \textbf{R3}
\end{itemize}
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Four signs arrived in the last three chapters, each riding behind one number. None of them is closed until it can be written with no chapter to prompt it.

\begin{enumerate}
\raggedright
  \item Write \textbf{\mw{इ}}, \textbf{\mw{ळ}}, \textbf{\mw{अ}} and \textbf{\mw{उ}} in a row from dictation, shuffled.
  \item Beside each, write the number that needed it — and only that number.
  \item Write \textbf{\mw{कोनी}} and \textbf{\mw{पाछे} \mw{मिलसू}}, which needed no new sign at all.
  \item Say which of the four signs is \emph{not} a vowel, and which language does not have it.
\end{enumerate}
